explain.say: Drive on a concrete motorway and you hear a steady da-dum, da-dum. Each beat is a joint between slabs. Concrete roads are called rigid pavements, and many built in Germany in the 1930s carried traffic for decades. On the board, one cut open: a thick concrete slab resting on thinner layers below.

explain.say: The concrete slab is the star. Unlike asphalt, it does not just pass the load down; it bends like a stiff plate and spreads a wheel over a wide area. The width it spreads over is the radius of relative stiffness. For a three hundred millimetre slab on a typical soil, it comes to about one metre.

explain.say: So how does rigid compare with flexible? The flexible road spreads load through its layers and is cheaper to build, but needs resurfacing every ten to fifteen years. The rigid road costs more at first and lasts thirty to forty. Which would you choose for a container port full of heavy lorries?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Rigid suits heavy traffic; flexible is cheaper first

explain.say: Rigid, for heavy loads! But concrete grows and shrinks with temperature. A slab four and a half metres long, warming by thirty degrees, grows by about one point three five millimetres. Without joints it would crack at random. Look at the groups: sawn contraction joints control cracking, and steel dowel bars across them pass the load from one slab to the next.

Westergaard showed in the 1920s that stresses are worst at the slab's edges and corners, which is why dowels and good support there matter so much. Well done! Challenge: a five metre slab warms by forty degrees. How much does it grow?

faq.a: A road made of a thick Portland cement concrete slab on a thin base and sub-base. The slab carries load by bending, like a stiff plate.

faq.q: What is the radius of relative stiffness?
faq.a: A length that describes how widely a concrete slab spreads a load: the fourth root of E h cubed over 12 times 1 minus mu squared times k. It is often close to 1 metre.

faq.q: What is the difference between flexible and rigid pavements?
faq.a: Flexible pavements spread load layer by layer through asphalt and granular layers; rigid pavements spread it by slab bending. Rigid costs more at first but usually lasts longer with less maintenance.

faq.q: Why do concrete roads have joints?
faq.a: Concrete shrinks as it cures and expands and contracts with temperature. Joints let slabs move and make cracks form at planned places instead of randomly.
asks: Purpose of joints in concrete pavement

faq.a: Smooth steel bars placed across transverse joints, free to slide on one side. They transfer wheel loads from one slab to the next while letting the joint open and close.

facts: H. M. Westergaard published his analysis of stresses in concrete pavement slabs in 1926.
Concrete expands by roughly 10 millionths of its length for each degree Celsius.
